It is listed as a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=shrine recorded in the Engishiki}}. {{nihongo|'''Sakahogi Shrine'''|坂祝神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mino Province]].

The name of Sakahogi Town is derived from this shrine.

Sakahogi Shrine, {{ill|Agatanushi Shrine (Minokamo)|ja|縣主神社 (美濃加茂市)|qid=Q11608132|lt=Agatanushi Shrine}} (Ōta Town, {{ill|Minokamo, Gifu|Q857305|qid=Q857305}}), and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamo Shrine}} ({{ill|Minokamo, Gifu|Q857305|qid=Q857305}}) are collectively referred to as the '''Three Kamo Shrines'''.

== Overview ==
The date of foundation is unknown. {{Citation needed|However, since the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mino no Kuni no Miyatsuko}} were imperial descendants following {{ill|Hikoimasu no Ōkimi|Q11487910|qid=Q11487910}}, there is a theory that the founding of Sakahogi Shrine dates back even earlier than the Heian period, when devotion to Kamo shrines flourished.|date=September 2020}} In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, Sakahogi was reportedly pronounced “Sakahafuri.”

{{Citation needed|According to Abe Einosuke’s *Nōhi Ryōkoku Tsūshi*, because the shrine’s name was Kamo Myōjin, when considered together with the enshrined deities of Kyoto’s {{ill|Kamigamo Shrine|Q700448|qid=Q700448|lt=Kamo Wakeikazuchi Shrine}} and {{ill|Shimogamo Shrine|Q701620|qid=Q701620|lt=Kamo Mioya Shrine}}, the enshrined deities of Sakahogi Shrine are presumed to be the same as those of Shimogamo Shrine: “{{ill|Tamayori-hime|Q56344982|qid=Q56344982|lt=Tadasu Tamayorihime no Mikoto}},” and her father deity, “{{ill|Kamotaketsunumi no Mikoto|Q11634939|qid=Q11634939}}.” There is also a theory that the Shikinaisha Sakahogi Shrine corresponds to the Hōri-be Shrine listed in the register, and that Sakahogi was also called Hōri-be. If this assumption is correct, Hōri-be would be the older term, and those Hōri-be may have been ritualists serving the nearby Agatanushi Shrine, or alternatively members of an immigrant clan from Wu listed in the Shinsen Shōjiroku. The former seems more plausible. In that case, it could also be inferred that the original deity of Sakahogi Shrine was the ancestral deity of the Hōri-be, who were closely connected to the Kamo Agata clan—descendants of Hikozai-no-Ō, the enshrined deity of Agatanushi Shrine.|date=September 2020}}.

In {{ill|1062|Q19396|qid=Q19396}} ({{ill|Kōhei|Q1193572|qid=Q1193572}} 5), during the {{ill|Former Nine Years' War|Q1187448|qid=Q1187448}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshitsuna|Q11564276|qid=Q11564276|lt=Kamo Jirō Yoshitsuna}} stopped at Sakahogi Shrine on his way to {{ill|Mutsu Province|Q907389|qid=Q907389}} as reinforcements for his elder brother {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|Q32613|qid=Q32613}}, and prayed for victory. One theory holds that Kamo Jirō felt a connection because Sakahogi Shrine stands on Mount Kamo. On his return from Mutsu Province, he is said to have stopped by again and constructed shrine buildings.

In {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 6), it became a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}} of Gifu Prefecture’s 10th large district, 11th small district.

On March 27, {{ill|1907|Q2048|qid=Q2048}} (Meiji 40), it was designated by the district head as a shrine receiving offerings of sacred food and heihaku.

In {{ill|1912|Q2077|qid=Q2077}} ({{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 1), the shrine buildings were damaged by a severe storm. The current buildings were reconstructed in {{ill|1914|Q2083|qid=Q2083}} (Taishō 3).

== Enshrined deity ==
* {{ill|Masakatsuyamatsumi-no-Kami|Q109368726|qid=Q109368726|lt=Masakatsuyamatsumi-no-Kami}} (Masakayama-tsumi-no-Kami)  
According to the *Kojiki*, when Izanagi slew Kagutsuchi (軻遇突智), the Eight Mountain Deities were born from Kagutsuchi’s body. This deity was born from Kagutsuchi’s head.

== Subsidiary shrines ==
Hakusan Shrine, Tsushima Shrine, Mikuwashi Shrine, Inari Shrine, Sarutahiko Shrine, Yamagami Shrine

== Location ==
* 1507-2 Sakakura, Aza Kamoyama, Sakahogi Town, Kamo District, Gifu Prefecture
